name: Quetiapine + Nortriptyline
summary: A combination of quetiapine (an antipsychotic) and nortriptyline (a tricyclic antidepressant) sometimes used off-label for depression with psychotic symptoms. It is not FDA-approved as a combination and has more side effects than either medicine alone.
description: Quetiapine is an atypical antipsychotic that blocks dopamine (D2) and serotonin (5-HT2A) receptors, among others, which helps with psychosis, steadies mood, and causes sleepiness. Nortriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant that keeps more norepinephrine and serotonin available in the brain. Used together, they may help with both depression and psychotic symptoms, but the combination is not FDA-approved and carries a higher risk of side effects, including sleepiness, dry mouth and constipation, and heart problems.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Quetiapine is an atypical antipsychotic that antagonizes dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors, among others, producing antipsychotic, mood-stabilizing, and sedative effects. Nortriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant that inhibits the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin, enhancing neurotransmission in the central nervous system. When used together, these agents may address both depressive and psychotic symptoms, though the combination is not FDA-approved and carries increased risk for adverse effects, including sedation, anticholinergic effects, and cardiovascular complications.
